record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Build a non-perturbative theory of functional integration in non-integer dimensions and explain why constructive analogs of the usual perturbative non-integer-dimensional tools are currently missing.

evidence.quote: Non-integer dimensions is an interesting perturbative tool... that has no constructive analog. One should understand why and build the non-perturbative theory of functional integration in non-integer dimensions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop a non-perturbative, mathematically rigorous theory of functional (path) integration in non-integer spacetime dimensions. Concretely:

1. Define, for any real parameter $d \in (0,\infty)\setminus\mathbb{N}$, a notion of "functional integral" or probability measure on a suitable space of fields that:
   (a) reduces to (or is consistent with) the standard Euclidean functional integration on $\mathbb{R}^n$ when $d = n$ is a positive integer;
   (b) admits a free Gaussian measure whose covariance is the Green's function of an elliptic operator (e.g. $(-\Delta + m^2)^{-1}$) interpolating in $d$, with controlled ultraviolet and infrared behavior;
   (c) supports interacting models obtained by inserting non-Gaussian potentials (e.g. $\phi^4$-type interactions) and proving non-perturbative existence of the resulting measure for at least some range of $d$ between standard integer dimensions.

2. Show that the perturbative expansion of correlation functions of this construction reproduces the formal dimensional-regularization expansion in $d$ used in perturbative quantum field theory (i.e. analytic continuation of Feynman amplitudes in the dimension parameter).

3. Explain the structural obstruction that has so far prevented such a construction: identify the precise reason why the standard constructive tools (cluster expansions, multiscale renormalization group analyses, lattice approximations, reflection positivity, Osterwalder–Schrader axioms, etc.), which all rely on an underlying integer-dimensional measure space, fail to admit analogs in non-integer dimensions, and propose a framework that overcomes this obstruction.
artifact.status_search_result: A non-perturbative constructive theory of functional integration in non-integer dimensions does not appear to exist in the literature. Standard references on constructive QFT (Glimm–Jaffe, Rivasseau, and surveys on nLab/Wikipedia) treat only integer spacetime dimensions, and dimensional regularization remains a purely perturbative tool. Some recent work (e.g. tree-formula approaches) has been suggested as a possible route, but no rigorous non-perturbative construction in non-integer dimensions has been reported.

status_evidence.title: Constructive quantum field theory - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Constructive results have been obtained for scalar field theory in dimensions 2 and 3, and Yang-Mills theory in dimension 3; non-integer dimensions are not addressed.
status_evidence.claim: Existing constructive QFT results are formulated only in integer dimensions.

status_evidence.title: Constructive Field Theory in Zero Dimension - Rivasseau
status_evidence.snippet: Tree formula approach is suggested as a promising route to study quantum field theory including non-integer dimensions in the future.
status_evidence.claim: Constructive treatment of non-integer dimensions is identified as a future research direction, not an achieved result.

status_evidence.title: Constructive Quantum Field Theory - Arthur Jaffe
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of constructive QFT focuses on integer-dimensional models; no construction in non-integer dimensions is described.
status_evidence.claim: Authoritative surveys do not report a non-perturbative construction in non-integer dimensions.
